newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to clear multi-billion dollar German aid plan.
newsitem.headline: EU to clear multi-billion dollar German aid plan.

text.p: After months of hard bargaining with Germany, the European Commission will clear on Wednesday a plan allowing Bonn to pour billions of marks into its regions over the next three years, Commission sources said on Monday.

The overall package involves seven billion European currency units ($8.68 billion) to be paid between 1997 and 1999, of which 90 percent will benefit the former east Germany, a Commission official told Reuters.

The agreement will keep state aid paid in the former west Germany at its current level despite a long and fierce battle by German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt to increase it to match huge subsidies in the east, the sources said.

To be eligible for aid, a region must suffer from high unemployment and have a gross domestic product below the national average. Although this is not a problem for the states which were under communist rule until 1990, many western regions included in the scheme appear to fail both tests, the sources told Reuters.
They nevertheless expected the German scheme to be approved because of the difficulties in reaching a compromise between Rexrodt and European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
"There has been a lot of arm wrestling over this," one source said.

Rexrodt had initially asked EU permission to help 22 percent of the population in west Germany but the Commission insisted that aid should remain within the current 20.8 percent level, the sources said.
"Germany argued extensively that it should increase the level of aid in the western regions to reduce the gap with the subsidies being paid in the east," another official said.
"This is ridiculous. This is like saying 'you must give me more because you are giving more to my neighbour' not because you need more," he added.
The huge level of subsidies being granted in Germany has met opposition not only from the Commission but also from other EU states.

The 1997-1999 scheme will be paid out of German, not EU coffers, although the Union will also contribute to regional development in Germany through its structural funds as it does for other European regions. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
